interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a negative surgical margin (0.0), no seminal vesicle invasion (0.0), absence of lymphovascular invasion (0.0), and a negative biopsy finding for high-grade disease, with the prostatectomy demonstrating a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 6.9 and the absence of lymph node removal, as nodal status is documented as pNx, which widens uncertainty. The difference between the biopsy and prostatectomy findings is noted, though the surgical pathology is the definitive post-operative finding. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data significantly limits the ability to track trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and subsequent changes would be crucial to refine this prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period around 78 months without an event. The fixed estimated horizon is 75.97 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 49.38–102.56 months; its coverage has not been validated.
